page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4 is a general-purpose server instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8481C cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz, the x86_64 processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance divergence between single-threaded and multi-threaded operations. Single-core performance sits in the average range, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1618.89 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1713.0. However, multi-core and memory subsystem benchmarks fall into the lower tiers. The stress-ng multi-core performance of 3315.66 and Geekbench multi-core score of 3813.0 are categorized in the bottom 25 percent, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression drops to the bottom 10 percent at 21.71 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached large-block read and write speeds measuring 28.42 GB/sec and 21.13 GB/sec respectively.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c3-standard-4 offers a standard resource density suitable for entry-level enterprise workloads that do not demand high parallel processing power or extreme memory throughput. The inclusion of advanced CPU instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, provides hardware-level acceleration for specific cryptographic and integer operations. This makes the instance appropriate for static web serving, which registers a throughput of 6.68 GB/sec, single-threaded file compression tasks, and lightweight text processing. It is less suitable for heavy database operations, software compilation, or multi-threaded physics simulations due to its lower multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmark ratings.

Consequently, this instance is qualitatively cost-effective for workloads with low parallelization requirements, such as static web hosting, single-threaded text processing, and basic cryptographic tasks, while being less optimal for memory-intensive databases or complex software compilation.
